Arkansas has introduced no AI legislation as of September 2026, making it one of the states that has not yet entered the policy record at all.

The absence of bills means there is no Arkansas-specific legal friction on AI deployment, data center permitting, or power procurement tied to statutory AI requirements. That is a neutral fact, not a sign of readiness or hostility. States with thin legislative records can move quickly in either direction once a single bill is introduced.

What the data does not cover is executive action, agency rulemaking, utility commission decisions, or local zoning choices that could affect the compute infrastructure Arkansas hosts or might attract. The legislative record is one layer of the policy environment, and here that layer is empty.
